assumptions.choice: Used the symmetric-crossover form (SMA9 crosses below SMA26) rather than the static SMA9<SMA26 state.
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly offers a choice ('SMA9 is below SMA26 (or SMA9 crosses below SMA26 if using symmetric crossover)'); the crossover form was chosen for structural parity with the long entry's SMA9-crosses-above-SMA26 condition.

assumptions.choice: Trailing-stop breach is detected via the bar's Low (for longs) / High (for shorts) touching stop_price, i.e. intrabar touch rather than close-only.
assumptions.reason: Spec doesn't state intrabar fill mechanics for the stop; Low/High touch is the literal reading of a price 'stop' and is distinguishable from the other close-based entry/exit conditions in the spec, while OHLCV Low/High are part of the given feed.

assumptions.choice: Stop-triggered exits are executed with self.close() (a market order), same as the cloud-based exit.
assumptions.reason: Canonical default: 'close the position' -> self.close(); no separate stop-order type is specified, so this avoids inventing additional order machinery.

assumptions.choice: stop_price is initialized on the entry bar using that bar's SMA26 (long: SMA26*(1-stop_pct), short: SMA26*(1+stop_pct)), then ratcheted every subsequent bar in the trade direction only.
assumptions.reason: Spec states the stop is 'updated each bar' but doesn't give its value at entry; initializing it at entry gives the stop a defined starting level as soon as a position opens.

assumptions.choice: When both the trailing stop and the cloud-based exit condition are triggered on the same bar, the stop is checked and acted on first.
assumptions.reason: Spec doesn't specify priority between the two exit mechanisms; checking stop first avoids submitting two close orders in the same bar.
